group: Walk disabled – exactly one matching schema

cases.expected: returns empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no errors, state.matchedNode set to true)
cases.description: state.isWalkEnabled() is false, the single registered schema validates without errors and state.hasMatchedNode() remains true, so numberOfValidSchema == 1 and the validator returns an empty error set.

cases.expected: returns Set containing OneOf ValidationMessage and the child ValidationMessage(s) from the failing schema
cases.description: state.isWalkEnabled() is false, the schema produces validation errors, therefore numberOfValidSchema stays 0, failFast is false, so a OneOf error is added together with the child errors.

group: Walk disabled – schema matches but state.hasMatchedNode is false

cases.expected: returns Set containing OneOf ValidationMessage (no valid schema counted)
cases.description: Even though the schema returns no errors, state.hasMatchedNode() is false after validation, causing the `continue` path; numberOfValidSchema remains 0, leading to a OneOf error.

group: Walk disabled – more than one matching schema

cases.expected: returns Set containing OneOf ValidationMessage (numberOfValidSchema == 2, short‑circuit after second schema)
cases.description: Two schemas both validate without errors, causing numberOfValidSchema to become 2, which triggers the break and later the OneOf error because exactly one schema must match.

group: Fail‑fast mode – invalid number of matching schemas

cases.description: failFast is true and the number of valid schemas is not exactly one, so the validator throws a JsonSchemaException instead of returning an error set.

group: Walk enabled – schema validation performed via walk()

cases.expected: returns empty Set<ValidationMessage> (schema.walk returns empty, state.hasMatchedNode true)
cases.description: When walk is enabled, the validator calls schema.walk(). The mock walk returns no errors and leaves state.hasMatchedNode true, resulting in a successful OneOf validation with no errors.

cases.expected: returns Set containing OneOf ValidationMessage (schema.walk returns empty but state.hasMatchedNode false)
cases.description: Even with walk enabled, if after schema.walk() the validator state reports no matched node, the schema is ignored (continue) and the final result is a OneOf error.

group: No schemas registered – always OneOf error

cases.expected: returns Set containing OneOf ValidationMessage (numberOfValidSchema == 0, childErrors empty)
cases.description: When the OneOfValidator has an empty schema list, the loop never increments numberOfValidSchema, so the validator must always produce a OneOf error regardless of the input node.

cases.expected: returns Set containing OneOf ValidationMessage and the child ValidationMessage(s) from errorSchema.walk
cases.description: With walk enabled, the validator calls schema.walk(). The mock walk returns a non‑empty error set, so numberOfValidSchema stays 0 and the final result contains the OneOf error plus the child errors.

group: Fail‑fast mode – exactly one matching schema

cases.expected: returns empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no exception, state.matchedNode true)
cases.description: Fail‑fast only throws when the OneOf condition fails. Here a single schema validates successfully, so the validator returns an empty error set even though failFast is true.

cases.expected: returns empty Set<ValidationMessage> (schema.walk called with validationEnabled=false, but still counts as valid, state.matchedNode true)
cases.description: When walk is enabled but the validator state reports validationEnabled = false, the schema.walk() is invoked with the flag false. The mock schema is set up to ignore validation when the flag is false and return an empty error set, leading to a successful OneOf validation.

group: Multiple schemas – first matches, second returns errors

cases.expected: returns Set containing OneOf ValidationMessage and child ValidationMessage(s) from errorSchema (numberOfValidSchema == 1, but childErrors from second schema are added)
cases.description: The first schema validates without errors, incrementing numberOfValidSchema to 1. The second schema produces errors; those errors are collected in childErrors and returned together with the OneOf error because exactly one schema must match, but additional errors from non‑matching schemas are also reported.

group: State.matchedNode reset between schemas – first matches but resets to false before second

cases.expected: returns Set containing OneOf ValidationMessage (numberOfValidSchema == 0 after second schema resets matchedNode)
cases.description: The first schema validates successfully and leaves state.matchedNode true, but the second schema explicitly sets state.matchedNode to false (simulated via mock). Because the loop continues, the first successful match is discarded, resulting in zero valid schemas and a OneOf error.

failFast is true and two schemas both validate without errors, so numberOfValidSchema becomes 2. The validator short‑circuits the loop and then throws a JsonSchemaException instead of returning an error set.
The method dereferences executionContext immediately to obtain CollectorContext; passing null triggers a NullPointerException.
The validator calls executionContext.getCollectorContext().enterDynamicScope(); if the collectorContext is null a NullPointerException is thrown.

group: Null schema element in schemas list

cases.description: During iteration the code invokes schema.validate on a null entry, causing a NullPointerException.
If a schema's validate method returns null, the subsequent call to schemaErrors.isEmpty() triggers a NullPointerException.
When walk is enabled the validator calls schema.walk; if that method returns null, the later schemaErrors.isEmpty() call throws a NullPointerException.
